ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the $4.50 no-show fee charged on TRP-03301 stands, and the driver is to be paid SGD 3.60.

Why the charge stands. POL-NS-01 requires four things and all four are on this record. (a) EV-TRIP-03301 carries the driver's 'arrived' event at 22:12:22. (b) EV-GPS-03301 places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from 22:12:22 - 42 accuracy-filtered in-radius fixes, far more than the three consecutive fixes POL-NS-02 requires, the first of them at the same instant as the marker. (c) The driver held position continuously for 410 seconds (22:12:22 to 22:19:12) against the 180-second free waiting period in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180; no_show_threshold_sec is null). (d) There is no boarding event, and the driver terminated the trip at 22:19:14 under RIDER_NO_SHOW, after the required dwell had elapsed at 22:15:22.

The arrival marker is not false. Under POL-NS-05 the test is the driver's position and speed at the marker: at 22:12:22 he was inside the radius and stationary, not more than 300 m away and not at 15 km/h or more, so the waiting clock is not recomputed. POL-NS-03 does not apply - his stationary fixes are inside the radius, not outside it but within 400 m. POL-NS-06 gives no relief: the 410-second dwell exceeds the 180-second minimum by 230 seconds, so there is no shortfall to refund, and the absent advisory is not needed because accumulation across separate intervals is not required for a single unbroken run.

The rider's arguments. I accept that the rider sent a message during the waiting window ('coming down now', 22:14:42) and that the driver neither replied within 120 seconds (though he read it at 22:15:12) nor placed an in-app call. But POL-NS-04 needs all three limbs, and limb (c) fails: the rider's own device track sits roughly 710-717 m from the pickup pin across all 62 fixes, far outside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, so the rider is not exonerated. POL-NS-11 does not rescue that finding - it applies where the rider track is absent or wholly filtered out, and here the track is present and admissible; limb (c) is failed, not undecidable. I also decline the request to escalate under POL-NS-09: the chat and the track do not contradict each other directly on rider presence - 'coming down now' is a statement of intention, and POL-NS-04(c) is the clause that resolves rider presence. The rider is right that the BUTTON arrival marker earns no POL-NS-12 platform-confirmation presumption, but the driver establishes POL-NS-02 on his own evidence regardless.

Driver compensation. The fee in force is SGD 4.50 (EV-FARE-03301, matching trip_record.platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd). Under POL-NS-07 the driver is paid 80 percent = SGD 3.60. The anti-farming check does not trip: no_show_terminations_30d is 1 (below 4) and 1 divided by 86 completed trips is about 0.012 (below 0.08), so compensation is paid rather than withheld.

Because the driver is owed money, the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION and amount_sgd carries the same SGD 3.60 figure under POL-GEN-03; the rider's $4.50 charge stands as it presently is. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-03301-01 (weight 0.0) carries no fact here, as nothing relied on it. The monetary effect, SGD 3.60, is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically on issue (POL-GEN-05).

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

This is a rider-filed NO_SHOW_CHARGE over the $4.50 cancellation fee. The fee stands, and the driver is paid $3.60.

To the rider: the record shows the driver did everything the no-show rule requires. All four limbs of POL-NS-01 hold. (a) The trip record carries the driver's own 'arrived' event at 11:58:03. (b) The GPS trace places him on the pin — minimum distance 0.157 m — with 42 fixes at the 25 m accuracy filter inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, the first at 11:58:03, so POL-NS-02 is satisfied. (c) He then held position continuously for 410 seconds, from 11:58:03 to 12:04:53, against the 180-second free waiting period in force (platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180). (d) No boarding is recorded and the driver terminated the trip under RIDER_NO_SHOW at 12:04:53, after the dwell had elapsed; no_show_threshold_sec is null, so no longer threshold defers that moment. The $4.50 charge reconciles exactly with platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd and the waiting-time line is 0.00, so there is no fare defect and no second charge to strip out.

Your 'coming down now' message at 12:00:23 does not exonerate you under POL-NS-04. That clause needs all three limbs, and its rider-presence limb (c) fails outright: your own track shows 70 fixes at roughly 645 m from the pin (min 642.1 m, max 648.7 m) and a qualifying-fix count of zero inside the 100 m STANDARD presence radius. The clause therefore does not apply, and the driver's silence after your message — which the record confirms, since trip_record.in_app_calls is empty — is noted but does not move the fee. POL-NS-05 (false arrival) does not bite either: at the arrival timestamp the driver was on the pin and stationary at 0.0 km/h, so the marker is true.

To the driver: your account is borne out by the platform's own telemetry, and your payout is fixed by POL-NS-07 at 80 per cent of the $4.50 fee, i.e. $3.60. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1 (below 4) and 1 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 86 is 0.012 (below 0.08). Because the compensation is paid, the ruling value is DRIVER_COMPENSATION and amount_sgd carries the same $3.60 — that is the amount the ruling moves, not a refund to the rider, whose $4.50 charge stands.

On the rider's escalation argument under POL-NS-09(c): I reject it. The clause requires two or more no-show disputes between the same rider and driver in 90 days. Each profile reports disputes_with_counterparty_90d = 1, and since the two of you are each other's counterparty on this trip, that is the same single dispute seen from both sides, not two. No other escalation trigger fires: the deciding facts rest on artifacts at weight 1.0, so confidence is 0.9, above the 0.70 floor; the trace, chat and fare records are complete and reconciled; the POL-NS-07 check does not trip; and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the 3 the clause reads.

On the two missing-advisory claims: EV-ADVIS-03302-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and both advocates disclosed that. Its absence only makes the dwell-accumulation limb of POL-NS-06(i) unavailable; the driver's single continuous 410-second dwell already exceeds the 180-second minimum, so nothing turns on it. On the profile point: POL-GEN-01 makes rating, prior_no_show_flags and the other listed fields context only, and none has been used against the rider here.

Confidence is capped by the deciding artifacts (EV-TRIP-03302 and EV-GPS-03302, each weight 1.0) at 1.0; I set it at 0.9. The monetary effect, $3.60, is below the $8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To the rider and the driver: this case does not end in an automatic payment to either of you. It is ESCALATED to a human reviewer, and the disputed SGD 4.50 is held — not collected from the rider and not refunded — until that review is decided. Escalation is terminal and replaces any money ruling, including the driver's payout.

WHAT THE EVIDENCE ESTABLISHES. The no-show is verified on the record. The driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 07:21:30 and the GPS trace's first qualifying in-geofence fix falls at that same second (dwell_start_offset_sec 0.0), inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, with the driver stationary — so the arrival marker is genuine, POL-NS-05 does not recompute the waiting clock, and no false-arrival referral arises. The driver then held position continuously for 410 seconds, to 07:28:20, against the 180-second free waiting period carried in this trip's platform_policy, and terminated at 07:28:24 under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW — 234 seconds after the required dwell had elapsed at 07:24:30. All four limbs of POL-NS-01 therefore hold: (a) an arrived event; (b) GPS presence in the geofence at or before it; (c) a 410 s dwell against 180 s; (d) no boarding, and a driver termination under a recognised no-show code after the dwell elapsed. No clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces the fee: the driver's stationary fixes lie inside the 50 m radius, not in POL-NS-03's 50–400 m wrong-entrance band (nearest approach 0.111 m), and there is no waiting-period shortfall under POL-NS-06. The rider's own track sits between 846.3 m and 854.2 m from the pin across all 74 fixes, far outside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, so POL-NS-04 limb (c) fails affirmatively and that clause does not exonerate the rider.

WHY THE CASE ESCALATES RATHER THAN PAYING THE DRIVER. With POL-NS-01 satisfied in full, POL-NS-07 would fix the driver's payout at 80% of the SGD 4.50 net fee — SGD 3.60 — but only if its anti-farming check is clear. It is not. The check reads only the trailing-window fields the clause names: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 5, which is 4 or more, and 5 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 40 is 0.125, which is greater than 0.08. Both limbs trip. Under POL-NS-07 the driver's compensation is therefore WITHHELD and the case escalates under POL-NS-09(d), which names precisely that anti-farming trip as a trigger. The lifetime counter driver_profile.prior_no_show_flags (9 on this record) is not the field this test reads and, per POL-GEN-01, is context only — it is used in neither direction here. Because escalation under POL-NS-09 is terminal, no monetary ruling issues, both money fields are null, and the disputed SGD 4.50 stays frozen.

REFERRAL. POL-NS-07 requires the escalation packet to direct the human reviewer to refund the rider's cancellation fee in full; that instruction is carried in the referrals list.

ON THE ADVOCATES' CLAIMS. The driver's case that the no-show is verified — the POL-NS-01 limbs (a) to (d), and the POL-NS-05, POL-NS-06, POL-NS-04(c), POL-NS-03 and POL-NS-10 points — is accepted on the facts and does not decide the outcome by itself. The driver's claim that POL-NS-07 pays SGD 3.60 and that the charge is 'not refundable on this trip's evidence' is outweighed by the driver's own accurate disclosure — matched by the rider's claim — that the same clause's anti-farming arithmetic trips on 5 and 40; where that check trips POL-NS-07 withholds the payout and routes the fee to POL-NS-09, so no DRIVER_COMPENSATION issues. The rider's claims that escalation is mandatory and terminal, and that nothing on his own profile engages POL-NS-09 (no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the 3-or-more threshold; disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0 on both sides), are accepted. The rider's POL-NS-04 point — limbs (a) and (b) met, limb (c) failed — is accepted and changes nothing: the driver's arrival and dwell stand on the GPS trace and trip record independently of it.

CONFIDENCE AND WEIGHT. Every artifact this ruling rests on — the trip record, GPS trace, chat log, fare ledger and driver profile — carries weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. The only artifact below 1.0 is the missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-03304-01 (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT); it carries no fact this ruling needs — no accumulation of separate in-geofence intervals is required and no advocate asserted it — so it neither caps nor discounts the finding, and it need not be narrated further. Confidence is 0.95, above the 0.70 floor; the escalation here is driven by POL-NS-09(d), not by low confidence.

OPEN QUESTION FOR THE REVIEWER. Whether this driver's five no-show terminations in the last 30 days against only 40 completed trips is the fee-farming pattern POL-NS-07's guard exists to catch, so that the rider's SGD 4.50 is refunded in full as the packet directs, or an ordinary work pattern on which the withheld compensation should be released instead. The monetary effect of either outcome (SGD 4.50) sits below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold, so the reviewer can release the held amount directly once decided.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-NS-07: direct the human reviewer to refund the rider's cancellation fee of SGD 4.50 in full — the anti-farming check on this driver has tripped, so the driver's compensation is withheld and the escalation packet must instruct the reviewer to make the rider whole.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the $4.50 is not being refunded and the driver is not being paid by this automated ruling — the case is going to a human reviewer, and the fee stays on hold. Here is why.

The no-show is verified on the merits. The trip record (EV-TRIP-03303) shows the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 11:00:27 and the 180-second free waiting period started at 11:00:29; he cancelled at 11:07:18 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-03303) places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius continuously for 410 seconds from 11:00:27, on 42 qualifying fixes — a surplus of 230 seconds over the 180 seconds required — and no longer threshold applies (no_show_threshold_sec is null). All four limbs of POL-NS-01 hold. There is no false-arrival point: the first in-geofence fix is at the arrival marker itself (offset 0.0 s) and he was stationary within the radius, so POL-NS-05 does not fire and no false-arrival referral is recorded.

The rider's refund routes do not open. POL-NS-04 fails at limb (c): the rider's device (EV-GPS-03303 rider track) sits 694–702 m from the pin on all 79 fixes, with zero qualifying fixes inside the 100 m STANDARD presence radius, so the clause does not exonerate her — and POL-NS-11 does not apply, because the track is present rather than absent. Her 11:02:47 'coming down now' message does not contradict the trace on rider presence: it is a forward-looking coordinating statement, and the records agree she was not at the pin, so POL-NS-09(b) is not engaged. POL-NS-03 does not apply (the driver's stationary fixes are inside the arrival radius, not outside it within 400 m). POL-NS-06 has no shortfall to work on. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-03303-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; it carries no fact and is not needed here.

What sends this to a reviewer is a repeat-dispute signal. Both profiles record 2 disputes with the counterparty in the trailing 90 days (EV-RPROF-03303 and EV-DPROF-03303, both weight 1.0). POL-NS-09(c) reads those two fields together and escalates where they show 2 or more no-show disputes between the same rider and driver; 2 meets that threshold. Escalation is terminal: no refund issues, no compensation issues, and the disputed $4.50 is held rather than collected or refunded.

For completeness: on the merits alone POL-NS-07 would have paid the driver 80% of the $4.50 fee in force, i.e. $3.60 (the figure the fare ledger itself carries), the anti-farming check not tripping — no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the count of 4, and 1/86 = 0.012, below the rate of 0.08. That $3.60 is part of what the reviewer decides. The fare ledger reconciles: the $4.50 charged equals the net fee in this trip's platform_policy, and POL-NS-08(d) also permits the $6.61 gross figure, so there is no fare-integrity defect. Every deciding artifact carries weight 1.0, so the confidence cap under POL-GEN-02(2) is 1.0 and confidence is set at 0.9 — not a trigger under POL-NS-09(a).

The reviewer should settle two open questions: (1) whether the two recorded counterparty disputes are in fact no-show disputes between this same rider and driver; and (2) whether, on the verified no-show, the driver's $3.60 payout should be released. The monetary effect at this stage is zero and the amount stays frozen.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

Escalated to a human reviewer; the disputed SGD 4.50 cancellation fee is held — not collected from the rider, not released — until that review.

TRIGGER. POL-NS-09(d) requires escalation where rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 3 or more. The rider's profile (EV-RPROF-03306) shows exactly 3 no-show disputes in the trailing 30 days, so the case goes to a person, and POL-GEN-03 makes that terminal: no money moves now. POL-GEN-01 permits this field to be cited for this limb and nothing else; the lifetime prior_no_show_flags figure (also 3) is NOT the field the limb reads and was not used by either side.

DRIVER'S CASE, RECORDED FOR THE REVIEWER. The trip record (EV-TRIP-03306) carries the driver's 'arrived' event at 11:17:19; the GPS trace (EV-GPS-03306) places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius in one continuous run of 42 qualifying fixes from 11:17:19 to 11:24:09 — a dwell of 410 s against the 180 s free waiting period in force (platform_policy.free_wait_sec) — and the trip was ended by the driver at 11:24:09 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW. On these artifacts POL-NS-01 limbs (a)–(d) read as satisfied and POL-NS-07 would pay the driver 80% of SGD 4.50 = SGD 3.60. His anti-farming check does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d = 0 against completed_trips_30d = 60). POL-NS-05 does not apply — the arrival marker is not false (closest approach 0.111 m; no 15 km/h motion at the marker) — and POL-NS-06's shortfall route does not open (shortfall −230 s). His claim that the emitted ruling should be DRIVER_COMPENSATION is therefore displaced by the mandatory escalation. His request that the packet DIRECT release of the SGD 4.50 and the SGD 3.60 is not something any clause authorises, so it is not issued as a referral; it is recorded here instead.

RIDER'S CASE, RECORDED FOR THE REVIEWER. POL-NS-04 limbs (a) and (b) are engaged — the rider sent 'coming down now' at 11:19:39 and the driver neither replied within 120 s nor placed an in-app call — but limb (c) fails, because her own device stayed 697–704 m from the pin with rider_qualifying_fix_count of 0, so POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate her. Her own submission concedes that limb, and the POL-NS-06 refund arithmetic is likewise closed. Her claim that the case must escalate under POL-NS-09(d) is accepted and is the ground of this ruling.

OPEN QUESTION FOR THE REVIEWER. Whether the three no-show disputes in the rider's trailing 30 days indicate abuse of the no-show process on her side (the limb's own basis for escalation), and, in light of that, whether the SGD 4.50 charge should stand and whether the driver's SGD 3.60 compensation should be released.

REFERRALS. None is issued: POL-NS-05(ii) does not fire (the arrival marker is not false), POL-NS-07's anti-farming direction to the packet does not fire, and no other clause produces a referral.

CONFIDENCE 0.90 — the escalating fact rests on EV-RPROF-03306, weight multiplier 1.0, which sets the POL-GEN-02(2) cap.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. The SGD 4.50 no-show fee stands, and SGD 3.60 of it is paid to the driver; you, the rider, receive no refund.

WHY THE FEE STANDS (POL-NS-01). All four conditions are on the record. (a) The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 10:16:33. (b) The GPS trace places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius at that moment: the first qualifying in-geofence fix is stamped 10:16:33 with dwell start offset 0.0, his closest fix is 0.0 m from the pin, and 42 of his 86 fixes qualify inside the radius - far past the three consecutive fixes POL-NS-02 requires. (c) He then held position continuously inside the geofence for 410 seconds (10:16:33 to 10:23:23), measured from the first qualifying fix as the clause requires, against the free waiting period of 180 seconds in force for this trip. That is a surplus of 230 seconds, not a shortfall. (d) No boarding event is recorded, and the driver terminated the trip at 10:23:23 under RIDER_NO_SHOW, after the required dwell had elapsed.

YOUR ACCOUNT, RIDER. 'Only a few minutes late' does not describe this record. Your own device track runs roughly 850 m from the pickup pin for the whole window (minimum 848.5 m, mean 852.3 m) and contains no fix inside the 100 m rider-presence radius. Your message at 10:18:53 ('coming down now') was a genuine coordinating message, and the driver neither replied within 120 seconds nor placed an in-app call before cancelling - POL-NS-04 limbs (a) and (b) are made out. But POL-NS-04 exonerates a rider only where limb (c) also holds, and limb (c) fails affirmatively on your own admissible fixes: you were not at the pin. On its own terms the clause does not apply, and the dispute is decided under POL-NS-01.

THE OTHER CLAUSES. POL-NS-05 does not fire: the 'I'm Here' tap is not a false marker - at that moment the driver was inside the radius and stationary, not more than 300 m away nor at 15 km/h or more - so the clock is the platform's, not a recomputed one, and no false-arrival referral arises. POL-NS-06 gives you nothing: the dwell is a single continuous 410-second interval with no shortfall to excuse, and the only traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-03305-01) is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, so limb (i) accumulation is unavailable in any event. POL-NS-03 does not apply, because the driver's stationary fixes lie inside the arrival radius rather than outside it. No POL-NS-08 integrity defect exists: no clock skew, no trace gap (100% coverage, max gap 0 s), the chat log matches the trip record's message count, and the fare line of SGD 4.50 reconciles with the SGD 4.50 figure in the platform policy. Nothing engages POL-NS-09: neither counterparty counter reaches 2, rider no_show_disputes_30d is 1 (below 3), and no artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence.

THE DRIVER'S PAYOUT (POL-NS-07). 80 percent of the SGD 4.50 fee is SGD 3.60, the residual 20 percent being the platform service fee, and the fare ledger's own derived figure agrees. The anti-farming check does not withhold it: no_show_terminations_30d is 4, so the count limb is met, but 4 divided by 60 completed trips is 0.067, not greater than the 0.08 the clause requires, and both limbs must trip. The lifetime counter prior_no_show_flags is not the field that check reads and is not relied on.

OUTCOME. Under POL-GEN-03 the rider's claim is not supported and the charge stands, while on a DRIVER_COMPENSATION ruling amount_sgd carries the same SGD 3.60 as driver_compensation_sgd - it is the amount the ruling moves, not a refund to the filing party. The monetary effect (SGD 3.60) is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically. No referral is produced, because no clause on these facts adds one. Confidence 0.9: the deciding facts are carried by the GPS trace, trip record, chat log and fare ledger, each at weight 1.0.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To the rider: the fee stands, and here is why. The driver marked himself arrived at 20:49:25 and the platform's own trace shows him inside the 50 m pickup radius in one continuous run of 42 position fixes from 20:49:25 to 20:56:15 — 410 seconds of waiting, measured from the first in-geofence fix and not from the tap (EV-GPS-03307, EV-TRIP-03307). The waiting period this trip allowed was 180 seconds (platform_policy.free_wait_sec), so he held position 230 seconds longer than required before cancelling at 20:56:19 under the code RIDER_NO_SHOW, with no boarding recorded. That satisfies all four conditions of POL-NS-01, so the $4.50 cancellation fee was chargeable — that is platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd, and the fare-breakdown line shows the same $4.50. None of the rider-side routes bite: POL-NS-06 needs a shortfall and there is a surplus of 230 seconds; POL-NS-05 needs a false arrival marker and the marker coincided exactly with the first in-geofence fix (dwell start offset 0.0 s, closest approach 0.25 m); POL-NS-03 concerns a driver stationary outside the radius, and this driver was inside it.

You are right that you answered the driver's 'where are you' with 'coming down now' at 20:51:45, and that the driver neither replied within 120 seconds nor logged an in-app call — those are limbs (a) and (b) of POL-NS-04. But that clause requires all three of its limbs, and its third reads your own device's track, which placed you about 773 m from the pin on every fix, with no qualifying fix inside the 100 m STANDARD presence radius (EV-GPS-03307). So POL-NS-04 does not exonerate you. It would make no difference if that test could not be run at all: POL-NS-11 says the clause then simply cannot help the rider, and the fee is decided on the driver's evidence. Your point that the chat message and the rider track pull in different directions does not send this to a human reviewer. Where your presence matters, the policy names the test that decides it (POL-NS-04(c), and POL-NS-11 if it cannot be run), and the fee itself does not depend on your presence — POL-NS-01 and POL-NS-06 both operate 'whether or not the rider was present'. A clause therefore resolves the point, so the POL-NS-09(b) trigger is not engaged, and no other POL-NS-09 trigger is present: both counterparty-dispute counters are 0, your no_show_disputes_30d is 1 (the limb reads 3), the anti-farming check is clear, and every artifact carrying a deciding fact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so limb (e) is not reached. The disputed fee is not held.

To the driver: POL-NS-07 fixes your payout at 80 percent of the net cancellation fee in force — 0.80 × $4.50 = $3.60, which is also the figure stated on the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-03307). The anti-farming check does not trip: no_show_terminations_30d is 0 against the absolute threshold of 4, so the accompanying rate test cannot bite either.

No artifact is impaired for policy purposes under POL-NS-08: the arrival event and the nearest trace fix agree to the second, the trace has no gaps and 100 percent coverage, the chat log holds the 2 messages the trip record records, and the cancellation-fee line reconciles with the figure the resolution rule produces. The only missing artifact, the traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-03307-01, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT), is not relied on for any finding, and the single continuous in-geofence run means no accumulation under POL-NS-06(i) was ever needed. Confidence is 0.90, against a cap of 1.0 set by the weight-1.0 artifacts the finding rests on. The money moved (SGD 3.60) is below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold. Ruling: DRIVER_COMPENSATION — the $4.50 charge stands and the platform pays the driver $3.60.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To both parties. Measured on the GPS trace (EV-GPS-03308, weight 1.0), this trip ran 14.4 km against the 9.0 km optimal route recorded at booking (EV-TRIP-03308), an excess of 5.4 km — 60% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass (over 20% of optimal and over 0.8 km absolute), and the excess also exceeds 50%, so the deviation is MATERIAL. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes: 114 fixes at a 10-second interval, no gaps, maximum gap 0 seconds, 100% coverage, so POL-RD-07(a)-(c) does not fire, no independent corroboration is required and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

The driver's explanation ('Road works.') cannot reduce the excess by a metre. No traffic advisory is on file for this trip: EV-ADVIS-03308-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so POL-RD-03's comparison cannot be run and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Because the driver named no advisory evidence ID, POL-RD-13 applies: the absent advisory is a gap in the bundle, not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged and this case does not escalate — the driver's contrary claim is rejected on that ground. POL-RD-04 is unavailable (the chat log EV-CHAT-03308 holds no messages and no waypoint to corroborate), POL-RD-05 has no amendment to re-baseline against, and POL-RD-11 and POL-RD-12 do not apply (fare model METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null; vehicle type RYDE_X).

The money. charged_total is $20.66 (EV-FARE-03308). Under POL-RD-02 the recomputed fare is (3.80 + 0.75 × 9.0 + 0.28 × 13.0) × the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, plus the 0.80 platform fee = $14.99; the POL-RD-02 partial refund is therefore $5.67, payable $5.70 after rounding up, which is above the $0.50 de minimis floor.
